author: PhatBoB
quote:
No one is questioning Rockstar’s technical work. Managing to get such a detailed world running on a PS5 is impressive—hats off to them. But are we judging a video game, or a tech demo?

I keep seeing videos celebrating the graphics, lighting, details, and realism, while gameplay, mission design, narrative pacing, and control responsiveness seem to take a back ****’re talking about a game with an astronomical budget, yet we still see objects magically spawning in characters' hands (have you tried buying a burger? Go ahead and try, then let me know), weapons sticking to backs like magnets, highly scripted missions, mundane interactions, and long sequences where the player does next to nothing. Not to mention the 30 FPS cap and technical issues—which don’t even seem to be factored in, even though for any other title, these would easily cost it a point or two in its final score.

Years ago, *Red Dead Redemption 2* already demonstrated an impressive level of care for certain animations and interactions. And *The Witcher 3* taught us that a game doesn’t need the best technical specs or the best combat system to be memorable; what it needs is strong writing, engaging missions, and gameplay that truly draws the player in.

I don’t mean to dismiss the merits of *GTA VI*, but everywhere I look, I see a great deal of confusion between technological excellence and excellence in game design. Everyone talks about "incredible depth," but I’d like to see concrete examples of this depth within the gameplay—not yet another video showing how realistic the puddles look.A video game must, first and foremost, be a *good* game. And that, in my view, is the question too many people are forgetting to ask.
